summary: Markets are climbing Friday as investors digest a hawkish policy backdrop following the Fed's first rate hike since 2023. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on September 16, with Chair Kevin Warsh signaling inflation remains elevated and 16 of 18 members expecting at least one more hike this year. FOMC minutes released October 7 confirmed a tilt toward further tightening. Meanwhile, stock markets are shaking off Thursday's tech selloff, sparked by reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue may be $20 billion lower than expected, raising fresh questions about AI valuations. Oil prices retreated after President Trump pledged not to attack Iran before the midterm elections, easing geopolitical pressure. Bitcoin is stabilizing around $82,400 after ETFs hemorrhaged $729 million over two days—the worst outflow stretch since June—amid rising Treasury yields and weakening risk appetite. Delta Airlines slashed guidance after missing Q3 earnings, and SpaceX's $8 billion spectrum deal sent telecom giants tumbling while tower operators surged. With September jobs data showing just 29,000 payrolls added and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey due at 10 AM, investors are balancing Fed hawkishness against softening macro data ahead of earnings season's peak in late October.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh signals more rate hikes as inflation remains elevated
signals.desc: The FOMC raised rates 25 bps in September and 16 of 18 members project at least one more hike this year, pressuring risk assets as the 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5.26%.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs see $729M outflow in two days, worst since June
signals.desc: US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $484.9 million on October 7 and $244.1 million on October 8, signaling institutional retreat as Treasury yields compete for capital.

signals.title: OpenAI revenue concerns trigger tech selloff, AI valuations under scrutiny
signals.desc: Reports that OpenAI's annualized revenue may be $20 billion below estimates sparked Thursday's tech decline, with chipmakers Nvidia down 2.9%, Broadcom down 4.6%, and Micron down 4.8%.

signals.title: Oil retreats as Trump pledges no Iran attack before midterms
signals.desc: President Trump's statement that the US will not attack Iran before November 3 elections sent crude prices lower, easing inflationary pressures and supporting equity markets Friday.

signals.title: SpaceX spectrum deal reshuffles telecom sector, tower stocks surge
signals.desc: SpaceX's $8 billion low-band spectrum acquisition sent Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile down over 7% while American Tower, Crown Castle, and SBA Communications surged on new build-out demand.

verdict: Stocks are bouncing on lower oil and tech recovery, but Fed hawkishness, crypto outflows, and AI valuation concerns keep bulls cautious ahead of late-October earnings.
